A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FRABench and evaluator research, with GenEval renamed UFEval. The main text, appendices A-G, tables, and figures support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluator benchmark results, training-order experiments, position-consistency measurements, and human-annotation agreement in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original evaluator experiments and reports additional Pickapic evaluations and training-mixture ablations.

M1.justification: Both versions use the 112-aspect taxonomy, matching aspect-conditioned evaluation prompts, and unified supervised fine-tuning of Qwen2-VL, including the retained 72B variant. Renaming the evaluator and newly specifying cross-entropy training and annotation details do not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: v3 adds Pickapic evaluation using 500 test samples representing real users' preferences over generated images (Appendix C; Tables 5 and 47). The existing FRABench tasks, sub-tasks, and other public benchmarks remain, making this a limited extension within image-generation evaluation.

E2.justification: v3 adds Auto-J and Prometheus 2 to the SummEval, MANS, and MT-Bench comparisons, including the 72B comparison table (Tables 3 and 48). Auto-J receives aggregate SummEval scores rather than individual aspect scores. This expands the NLG comparator set while retaining the established multimodal baselines.

E3.justification: v3 introduces IU-only, IG-only, ITIG-only, and paired-task training configurations evaluated on FRA-ID and public benchmarks. It removes the six sequential modality-order configurations evaluated in v1 Appendix D.2 and adds the Pickapic testing protocol. These substantially revise the experimental controls; common benchmark settings and the principal fine-tuning recipe remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New training-mixture ablations investigate whether joint learning improves benchmark performance and individual evaluation aspects (v3 Tables 4-5, Figure 4, and Tables 52-54). The staged-training and forgetting analysis in v1 Figure 14 and Table 48 is removed. Position-bias, aspect-diversity, universal-aspect generalization, scaling, and qualitative-case evidence remain.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same three-annotator agreement tables, and neither reports model-performance confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-run uncertainty. v3 adds an aggregate agreement value in prose without changing the underlying statistical reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Pickapic, new NLG baseline, and training-mixture results add substantial evidence, while staged-training results disappear. The 16 detailed FRA accuracy tables remain unchanged. Qwen2VL-72B's WildVision accuracy with ties changes from 67.3 to 50.3 (v1 Table 5; v3 Table 4), and reported in-domain aggregates are revised despite unchanged component tables; these revisions do not demonstrate improved evaluator performance.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theorems, proofs, or mathematical derivations. The taxonomy and generalization arguments remain descriptive and empirical; the newly stated standard cross-entropy loss does not introduce a theoretical contribution.

C1.justification: v1 foregrounds explicit aspects as a route to objectivity, a first large-scale multimodal evaluation resource, and transfer to unseen tasks and modalities. v3 removes the objectivity and unseen-modality claims, emphasizes a first unified evaluator with task and aspect generalization, and makes mutual benefits from joint task/aspect learning a central contribution.

C2.justification: v3 develops concrete interpretations of cross-task synergy and shared aspect knowledge, and explains transfer of selectively sampled universal aspects. It removes v1's substantive discussion of harmfulness over-association, weak visual perception and fidelity assessment, and the 7B model's cost advantage over 72B, although the underlying failure cases and scaling results remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds a dataset access link, changes the code pointer, supplies the GPT-4o feedback template for human-scored images (Table 59), and explains loss coverage and response-order balancing. It also reports checking training/meta-benchmark overlap. These extend documentation; the main hardware, framework, and training hyperparameters were already disclosed in v1.

R1.justification: v3 adds Pick-a-Pic and Wang et al.'s unified reward-model reference, while removing BIGGen-Bench and the discussion rejecting automatically generated ultra-fine aspects. Most substantive related-work comparisons remain, with headings and positioning refocused on limitations of task-specific evaluators.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Related Work moves before Methodology, construction and training sections are consolidated, in-domain discussion moves into Appendix D, and public-benchmark results are organized by NLG, IU, and IG. This materially changes the narrative structure.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column main layout, combines the two aspect-tree figures into an illustrated evaluation pipeline, merges benchmark tables, and adds training-mixture displays while removing the staged-training display. Numerous retained figures and tables are relocated and resized; their relocation does not represent new evidence.

improvement.justification: The new same-backbone training-mixture ablations support joint-training benefits more directly than v1's comparisons between different evaluators. Added NLG comparators and annotation/data-access disclosures also strengthen evaluation and reproducibility. These gains are tempered by removal of staged-training evidence and explicit failure/cost discussion, plus new overstatements: v3 says only Claude beats UFEval on MT-Bench, although Table 3 also places Qwen2VL-72B above it.
